todo: Evidence review did not identify sufficiently direct, high-quality evidence to retain OCD-to-OSA or OCD-to-GERD as routine suggestions; these pathways should remain excluded unless stronger evidence is identified.

suggestions.rationale: Published clinical research has reported higher obsessive-compulsive symptoms among people with migraine, but the evidence is limited and does not establish that OCD caused or aggravated an individual veteran's migraine disorder. The application should therefore treat this as a possible association requiring case-specific medical evidence rather than a presumed nexus.
evidenceGaps: Clinician-documented migraine diagnosis and headache history
Documentation establishing the OCD diagnosis, severity and timing relative to migraine onset
Neurology or other qualified medical opinion addressing causation or aggravation in the individual case

sourceReferences.note: Clinical study evaluated OCD in migraineurs and reported an association in the studied population; it does not establish individual-level causation or aggravation.
Legal framework for secondary service connection and aggravation; it is not medical evidence establishing an OCD-to-migraine nexus.
